markets.rules_primary: If the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) national organization publicly endorses Shawn Fain in the 2028 presidential election, including the Democratic primaries before Mar 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
An endorsement requires a clear, affirmative statement of support for the candidate's election in the 2028 presidential election, including the Democratic primaries, made after Issuance and before Mar 1, 2028. The statement must be public (not private communications) and must specifically reference that race or be clearly in context of it. The endorsement must come directly from DSA or through its official channels.

The following scenarios would resolve to YES:
DSA states that it endorses the candidate for president
DSA states that it supports the candidate, with clear reference to the race
DSA releases an official endorsement through its national channels
DSA allows its name or logo to be used in the candidate's campaign materials

Positive comments without explicit support, or policy endorsements without a candidate endorsement, do not qualify. Ranking a candidate anything other than first in a ranked-choice process does not qualify, and publication of poll or ranked-choice results, whether national or chapter-level, is not itself an endorsement; only the resulting decision of the national organization qualifies. Social media endorsements count only from verified accounts, and likes or retweets alone do not constitute endorsement. Quote tweets with additional supportive commentary do count. Statements of obvious sarcasm, or which are immediately followed by clarifications that DSA is joking, are not encompassed by the Payout Criterion.

Only the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) national organization satisfies the Payout Criterion, acting through its national governing bodies or processes and announced through DSA's national channels. Qualifying decisions include a resolution or vote of the DSA National Convention, a decision of the National Political Committee, and a binding vote of the national membership. An endorsement, chapter poll result, or statement of support from a local or state DSA chapter, caucus, or working group does not qualify unless the national organization adopts it.

A statement that a candidate has or will have DSA's endorsement qualifies if the only condition attached is that the candidate enter or remain in the race. A statement conditioned on anything else, such as winning a primary or adopting a policy position, does not.

The Contract shall resolve immediately upon confirmation of the first qualifying endorsement. If DSA endorses more than one listed candidate, each endorsed candidate's strike resolves Yes at a value of ($1.00 / N) rounded down to the nearest $0.01, and all non-endorsed named-candidate strikes resolve No. If no qualifying endorsement occurs before Mar 1, 2028, the "No one" strike resolves Yes and every named-candidate strike resolves No. An endorsement of a candidate who is not listed resolves every market No.

If a candidate withdraws from, suspends their campaign for, ceases to be a candidate in, declines to enter, or loses the primary or general election for the race before a qualifying endorsement of that candidate is confirmed, their strike may resolve to No in the sole discretion of the Exchange.

markets.rules_primary: If physical construction work on federal border security infrastructure inside Big Bend National Park resumes after Issuance and before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Only reporting from any of the Source Agencies qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

Only work inside the boundary of Big Bend National Park counts. Activity elsewhere along the border, including elsewhere in the Big Bend Border Patrol sector and on state or private land, is outside this market.

Federal border security infrastructure means patrol and access roads, vehicle barriers, fencing or wall, detection technology, surveillance towers, lighting and power lines installed for border security purposes. Work on any one component is enough, and it does not matter how the work is characterised by the agency or its contractors.

Qualifying work is physical: disturbing ground, or erecting or installing any of that infrastructure.

The following do NOT satisfy the Payout Criterion:
Surveying, mapping, environmental review or planning that does not disturb ground
Moving or staging equipment without physical work starting
Restoration, revegetation or remediation of ground disturbed before the pause
An announcement that work will resume on a future date

Oral rulings from the bench unless reduced to a written order

markets.rules_primary: If CMS announces the addition of GLP-1 drugs for obesity to Part D before Jan 20, 2029, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
GLP-1 drugs are already covered under Part D for type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular risk reduction and obstructive sleep apnea. Those indications are outside this market, which turns on coverage for obesity or chronic weight management.

Only a completed CMS action that provides the coverage counts, such as a final rule, a finalized model design, or guidance to Part D sponsors through the Health Plan Management System. Where the White House or HHS makes the determination, the CMS document adopting it resolves this market, on the date of that document.

The following do NOT resolve this market to YES:
A CMS communication that discusses, studies or reports on such coverage.
A proposed rule or a request for applications, which propose coverage rather than provide it.
An action that considers the change and declines to make it.
The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge, or extending or replacing it, because it sits outside the Part D benefit.
An announcement covering only the Medicaid portion of the BALANCE Model.

Coverage of a single drug, or of a subset of Part D enrollees, is sufficient. The announcement date governs, not the date coverage takes effect.
